Neighborhood: Albany (San Pablo Ave near Solano Ave)
Directory Description: 310 Eatery brings the flavors of Los Angeles street and comfort food to San Pablo Avenue in Albany. Owner Aaron Fong got his start in restaurants as a server at Grazzy Burgers, the burger spot that once occupied this same address, and he launched 310 Eatery in Walnut Creek in 2014 before reopening it here in 2018. The menu centers on burgers and beer, with playful LA-inspired creations such as the 405 Traffic Jam Burger, bacon jam fries, and a Little Tokyo Po' Boy built on soft-shell crab with unagi aioli. It is a casual stop for dine-in, takeout, or delivery.
Highlights: 405 Traffic Jam Burger; bacon jam fries; Little Tokyo Po' Boy (soft-shell crab, fried egg, spicy slaw, unagi aioli); burgers and brews
Notes to Verify: Full name per Google/Waze listing is '310 Eatery- LA Style Street Food'. Address is Albany (94706), not Berkeley. No standalone official website found; Instagram/Facebook used (a mybistro.online page appears to be third-party). Phone from input; not independently confirmed. Owner/history details come from 2018-era Beyond the Creek coverage; Yelp listing active as of Aug 2026. Menu items may have changed since 2018.

Cuisine: American breakfast, brunch and lunch / comfort food
Directory Description: Tucked into a pink-fronted corner building at Grayson and Seventh streets, 900 Grayson is a longtime West Berkeley favorite for breakfast and lunch. The kitchen puts creative spins on American comfort food, drawing on quality, seasonal ingredients and the occasional Asian accent. It has long been known for the Demon Lover, a plate of spicy fried chicken over buttermilk waffles, along with a natural-beef burger topped with applewood-smoked bacon and house barbecue sauce. The low-key, neighborly room fills quickly on weekdays and Saturday mornings, and outdoor seating and takeout are also available.
Highlights: The Demon Lover (spicy fried chicken and buttermilk waffles); natural beef burger with applewood-smoked bacon and house BBQ sauce; creative breakfast plates; outdoor seating
Hours: Mon-Fri 8-10:45am (breakfast), 11:30am-2pm (lunch); Sat 8am-2pm; Sun closed (per Visit Berkeley; verify)
Notes to Verify: Owner/chef info (co-owners Anthony and Christopher Saulnier; dishes Demon Lover, Ladyboy, Gollum) comes from a 2012 Berkeleyside article and may be dated; omitted names from description. Listings (Yelp Sept 2026, OpenTable 2026, Visit Berkeley) indicate it is operating. Official site did not render details in fetch.

Directory Description: Angeline's Louisiana Kitchen is Downtown Berkeley's slice of New Orleans, set on Shattuck Avenue at Kittredge Street near the downtown theaters and BART. Founder Robert Volberg opened it to share Southern hospitality and Louisiana flavors with the Bay Area, and the menu leans on Big Easy classics: jambalaya, gumbo, buttermilk fried chicken, Creole barbecue shrimp, and beignets for dessert, with Abita beer to wash it down. The casual, kid-friendly dining room comes with New Orleans music, and there is outdoor seating in warmer months. Dine-in, takeout, and delivery are all available.
Highlights: Jambalaya; gumbo; buttermilk fried chicken; Creole barbecue shrimp; beignets; Abita beer; New Orleans music
Notes to Verify: Owner Robert Volberg and executive chef Brandon Dubea named in KQED Check, Please! info page (originally 2008, updated Sept 2024) and ABC7; chef not included in description in case of turnover. Opening year not confirmed. Active Toast ordering and Yelp listing updated Sept 2026.

Directory Description: Anja's is a small German cafe from chef Anja Voth, who ran the beloved Gaumenkitzel on San Pablo Avenue for 13 years before closing it in 2024. Working with her husband, Kai Flache, she reopened on University Avenue that summer with a lighter, daytime menu she describes as California cooking with German love, built on organic and sustainable ingredients from her longtime suppliers. Expect creamy oat porridge, savory potato-egg muffins, soups, and German sheet cakes such as poppyseed and apple, plus Gugelhopf. Guests can linger on the patio beside rose gardens or grab something to go.
Highlights: Oat porridge; potato-egg muffins with beets or smoked salmon; German sheet cakes (poppyseed, apple, seasonal plum); Gugelhopf; patio among rose gardens; chef-owned
Hours: Tue-Sat 8:30am-3pm (as reported at 2024 opening; verify)
Notes to Verify: Opened late Aug 2024. Visit Berkeley lists it as 'Anja's Kitchen'; Yelp and Downtown Berkeley list 'Anja's'. anjaskitchen.com may be a legacy Gaumenkitzel-era domain - verify. Phone from input, not independently confirmed. Dinner service was planned in 2024; unconfirmed. Yelp listing updated July 2026.

Directory Description: Ashby Eatery is a relaxed neighborhood cafe on Adeline Street, directly across from the Ashby BART station, that opened in fall 2025 in the former Flacos space. It serves elevated breakfast and lunch all day, from biscuit egg sandwiches, the Berkeley Scramble, and banana bread French toast to a spicy honey fried chicken sandwich, a vegan BLTA, grain bowls, and kale Caesar salad. Smoothies, coffee, beer, and wine round out the drinks, and there is a kids' menu plus happy-hour tacos and snacks. Covered and open-air seating make it an easy stop, and dogs are welcome.
Highlights: Spicy honey fried chicken sandwich; banana bread French toast; biscuit egg sandwich; Berkeley Scramble; vegan BLTA; smoothies; happy hour; dog-friendly outdoor seating
Hours: Wed-Thu & Sun 8am-4pm; Fri-Sat 8am-7pm; Mon-Tue closed (per Toast ordering page)
Notes to Verify: Input described it as fried chicken/American; menu is broader breakfast-lunch with a fried chicken sandwich. Owners not identified in any source. Opened ~Oct 2025. No standalone website found; Instagram used.

Neighborhood: Upper Solano Ave / Thousand Oaks (at The Alameda)
Directory Description: Bangalore Blues is the sit-down evolution of Pochys, restaurateur Aravind Pochiraju's South Indian spot on Solano Avenue, reborn in early 2026 with a dining room awash in deep blue down to the plates. The kitchen draws on Bangalore street food and home cooking, roasting whole spices in-house and making its own ghee. Look for crisp masala and ghee dosas, soft idli, Chicken 65, gobi Manchurian, kathi rolls, and donne biryani made with seeraga samba rice. For a deeper dive, an $80 multi-course Karnataka tasting menu features dishes such as koli saaru and chicken chops.
Highlights: Masala and ghee dosas; idli; donne chicken biryani (seeraga samba rice); Chicken 65; gobi Manchurian; kathi rolls; $80 Karnataka tasting menu
Hours: Tue-Sun 11am-3pm and 4-9pm (Hoodline, Apr 2026); pochys.com says closed Thursdays - verify
Notes to Verify: Same address as Pochys; Richmondside describes Pochys as relocated/rebranded as Bangalore Blues, Hoodline calls it the sit-down evolution of Pochys. Website is still pochys.com (reservations/ordering). Phone from input, not independently confirmed. Tasting menu price as of Apr 2026. Address is Berkeley 94707 (Solano Ave at The Alameda).

Neighborhood: West Berkeley (Aquatic Park area, near Berkeley Bowl West)
Directory Description: Bangkok by the Bay is a family-run Thai restaurant that opened in November 2024 in West Berkeley's Aquatic Park district, in the tree-lined courtyard space long home to Riva Cucina. Co-owners Sung Makawatsakul, who leads the kitchen, and Nantika Julakasilp serve familiar favorites alongside dishes less often seen on Bay Area menus. Standouts include laab gai presented in a purple cabbage leaf, a massaman curry of slow-cooked bone-in short ribs, and carefully garnished pad Thai. The bright dining room and large outdoor patio suit weekday lunches, happy hour, dinner, and private events.
Highlights: Laab gai in purple cabbage leaf; short-rib massaman curry; pad Thai; large outdoor patio; happy hour; private events and catering
Hours: Mon-Fri lunch 11:30am-2:30pm, happy hour 5-6pm, dinner 5-8:30pm; Sat happy hour 4:30-5:30pm, dinner 4:30-9pm (per official site)
Notes to Verify: Official site hours differ slightly from East Bay Express opening coverage (Mon-Fri 4-8:30pm dinner). Sunday hours not listed.

Directory Description: Brezo is a chef-owned California-Mexican restaurant on lower Solano Avenue in Albany, run by co-chefs Heather Mervine and Hector Hernandez. After starting in Point Richmond in 2017, the pair moved in early 2024 to the former Rendez-Vous Cafe Bistro space, where Mervine had begun her executive chef career, bringing her story full circle. The kitchen makes its own non-GMO masa, bakes pastries in-house, and cooks with seasonal California produce. Favorites include chilaquiles verdes, blueberry pancakes with blueberry butter, gorditas, braised lamb, and the Brezo Burger, served for brunch, lunch, and dinner indoors or on a sunny patio.
Highlights: Chilaquiles verdes; blueberry pancakes with blueberry butter; gorditas with house masa; braised lamb; Brezo Burger; house-baked pastries and desserts; sunny patio
Hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 10:30am-2:30pm & 5:30-8pm; Fri 10:30am-2:30pm & 5:30-9pm; Sat 8:30am-2:30pm & 5:30-9pm; Sun 8:30am-2:30pm & 5:30-8:30pm (per official site)
Notes to Verify: Located in Albany (94706), not Berkeley. Site styles the name 'Brezo_Restaurant'; 'Brezo' used as official name. Featured on KQED Check, Please! Bay Area.

Restaurant: Califa's Greens (styled "Califas Greens" on its website)
Cuisine: Latin American / Mexican; healthy bowls, salads and fresh juices
Directory Description: Califa's Greens is a family-run scratch kitchen on University Avenue. Owners Zeiri Guzman, Annia Guzman and Margarito Gallardo worked at La Capilla, the restaurant that used to occupy the space, and took it over in early 2021. The menu mixes fresh, vegan-friendly bowls and salads with Mexican and Latin American comfort food: kale and beet bowls, cochinita pibil and carnitas tacos, chilaquiles, huevos rancheros and enchiladas, all served with housemade salsas. Fresh-squeezed juices and smoothies go well with the lighter plates, and churros, alfajores and tres leches cake round things out. It's a relaxed, welcoming stop for breakfast, lunch or an early dinner.
Highlights: Kale and beet bowls; cochinita pibil and carnitas tacos; chilaquiles and huevos rancheros; housemade salsas; fresh juices and smoothies; churros, alfajores and tres leches
Hours: Sun 10am-3:30pm; Mon-Tue 10am-7:30pm; Wed 10am-3:30pm; Thu-Sat 10am-8:30pm (per website; Visit Berkeley lists slightly different hours)
Notes to Verify: The input called it Peruvian/Mexican, but no Peruvian dishes turned up; sources describe it as Mexican/Latin American and vegan-friendly. The website omits the apostrophe, while Facebook and Instagram use "Califa's Greens". Opened Jan 19, 2021.

Directory Description: Chez Mansour is a Lebanese and Mediterranean restaurant and wine bar on Solano Avenue in Albany, with an old-fashioned, candlelit dining room made for lingering. The kitchen makes its mezza in house, including hummus, baba ghannouge, falafel and grape leaves, which work well shared over a glass of wine. There are also grilled kababs of lamb, beef, chicken and seafood, shawarma, lamb chops, and baked eggplant with pomegranate sauce, with baklava to finish. Some evenings bring live music, including jazz duos and occasional belly dancing. Tables outside on Solano are a nice option on warm days.
Highlights: House-made mezza platter; grilled kababs and lamb chops; chicken shawarma; baked eggplant with pomegranate sauce; baklava; wine bar with live music some evenings; outdoor seating
Hours: Daily 11:30am-9:30pm (per official website; OpenTable shows a weekday afternoon break, 2:30-4:30pm)
Notes to Verify: No source confirms the "1920s-style" theme; sources call it old-fashioned and candlelit. ZIP: official site says 94707, while OpenTable and AAA say 94706 (Albany). OpenTable names the owners as "Mansour and Tanya" (first names only, unverified), so they're left out of the description.

Directory Description: Chez Panisse is Alice Waters' landmark North Berkeley restaurant and one of the places most closely tied to Californian cuisine and the farm-to-table movement. The kitchen cooks from peak-season produce and local sources, and the menus change every day. Downstairs, the main dining room serves a four-course set dinner in two nightly seatings, with the open kitchen and wood-burning oven in full view at the back. Upstairs, the more casual café offers an à la carte menu at lunch and dinner. It's a place food lovers seek out on purpose, and reservations open a month ahead.
Highlights: Four-course prix fixe downstairs; à la carte café upstairs; daily-changing seasonal menus; wood-burning oven and open kitchen; Alice Waters' flagship
Hours: Restaurant: Mon-Sat, two dinner seatings. Café: lunch Tue-Sat, dinner Mon-Sat. Closed Sunday.
Notes to Verify: The official information page lists (510) 548-5049 for pre-payments (10am-6pm); the input number (510) 548-5525 is kept as the main line. Adds a 17% service charge; reservations via the website or Resy, one month ahead.

Cuisine: Northwestern Chinese; Lanzhou hand-pulled noodles and BBQ
Neighborhood: Telegraph Avenue / Southside, near UC Berkeley
Directory Description: DH Noodles and Grill opened on Telegraph Avenue in spring 2026 and serves the regional cooking of Northwestern China. The focus is Lanzhou-style hand-pulled noodles, served in rich soups, tossed dry or stir-fried. The menu also has heartier dishes such as da pan ji, a big plate of chicken stew, and cumin-spiced lamb, plus Northwest-style grilled skewers, cold appetizers, and fried rice and pilaf. A few blocks from campus, it's a casual spot for a filling bowl of noodles at lunch or dinner, and it also does takeout and delivery.
Highlights: Lanzhou hand-pulled noodle soup; dry and stir-fried hand-pulled noodles; da pan ji (big plate chicken); spicy cumin lamb; Northwest BBQ skewers; cold dishes
Hours: Mon-Fri 11:30am-3:30pm & 4:30-8:45pm; Sat-Sun 11:30am-8:45pm (per Chowbus)
Notes to Verify: Full name confirmed as DH Noodles and Grill; Grubhub lists it as "DH Noodles and Grill Dun Huang Lan Zhou Niu Rou La Mian" (DH is probably Dun Huang, unconfirmed). No official website found, so the Chowbus ordering page is used. Owners unknown, and couldn't confirm whether it's independent or part of a group. It opened around May 2026.

Directory Description: Divan is a modern Turkish restaurant on Fourth Street that opened in June 2026, run by the team behind San Francisco's Taksim. The name refers to the central seating area of a traditional Turkish home, and the idea is hospitality: plates meant for sharing and taking your time over. The menu includes mezze such as hummus and muhammara, pide flatbreads, kebabs, cabbage rolls and grilled branzino, plus a generous Turkish breakfast for two with menemen and çılbır. The bright space has wood and tile details, a full bar with craft cocktails and sangria, and a covered patio.
Highlights: Mezze trio (hummus, muhammara, ezme); pide including sucuklu; kebabs such as çökertme kebabı; Turkish breakfast for two; house baklava; olive oil martini and house sangria; covered patio
Hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11:30am-2:30pm, Sat-Sun 11am-2:30pm; dinner daily 5-8:45pm (per website)
Notes to Verify: New, opened June 22, 2026 in the former Pollara space. Run by the Taksim (SF) team, so it's a Bay Area operator rather than a single-location Berkeley business. It started as lunch-only, and the website now lists dinner hours.

Address: 10172 San Pablo Ave, El Cerrito, CA 94530
Directory Description: Dolly's is a family-owned Italian restaurant and wine bar on San Pablo Avenue in El Cerrito, run by owner Dolly Batathota. Its signature dish is fettuccine finished tableside in a 100-pound wheel of Parmigiano-Reggiano, an idea Batathota brought home from a trip to Florence. It's served plain or topped with smoked salmon or prosciutto, and it's become the restaurant's best-known draw. The rest of the menu covers Italian classics, with a selection of wines to go with them. Dolly's also caters weddings, birthdays and corporate events, and offers takeout and delivery.
Highlights: Cheese-wheel fettuccine finished in a Parmigiano-Reggiano wheel; smoked salmon or prosciutto toppings; Italian wine selection; event catering
Notes to Verify: The website calls it "Dolly's Restaurant" and uses the domain dollystavern.com; Tripadvisor lists "Dolly's Tavern". Phone and ZIP 94530 come from the input and standard El Cerrito ZIP, not a fetched source. Hours not confirmed. Opening year not confirmed (probably 2023).

Directory Description: Duo Grill House is a neighborhood breakfast and lunch spot on Solano Avenue in Albany, serving hearty morning plates every day until mid-afternoon. Benedicts are a specialty, with five versions ranging from the classic to smoked salmon and a hash-topped take. There are also omelettes and scrambles (including one named for Albany), steak and eggs, Belgian waffles, and fried chicken and waffles. For something with more kick, there's a smothered breakfast burrito, chilaquiles and huevos rancheros. Egg plates come with Parmesan roasted potatoes or hash browns, and the counter now serves espresso. Dine in, take out or order delivery.
Highlights: Five eggs benedicts; omelettes and scrambles; steak and eggs; Belgian waffles and chicken and waffles; wet breakfast burrito and chilaquiles; Parmesan roasted potatoes; espresso
Hours: Daily 8am-3pm (per website)
Notes to Verify: No owner or backstory information found. Takes reservations through OpenTable and offers online ordering.

Restaurant: El Mono | Fresh Flavors of Peru
Address: 11720 San Pablo Ave, Suite B, El Cerrito, CA 94530
Directory Description: El Mono brings the bright, homestyle flavors of Peru to San Pablo Avenue in El Cerrito. Owners Matt Khadivian and Daniela Diaz built a lively, colorful dining room decorated with art inspired by the Nazca Lines. The rotisserie chicken is the signature, and the menu covers Peruvian classics such as lomo saltado and ají de gallina, a creamy chicken stew made with ají amarillo. Fried green plantains with chimichurri and yuca with rocoto aioli are popular starters. Guests can dine in, reserve for larger parties, or order takeout, and the restaurant also caters group events. A second El Mono has since opened on Fourth Street in Berkeley.
Highlights: Rotisserie chicken; lomo saltado; ají de gallina; fried green plantains with chimichurri; yuca with rocoto aioli; catering for groups; loyalty club
Notes to Verify: The address includes Suite B. The input phone 510-778-8884 is the main line; the El Cerrito direct line is 510-680-2910. A second location is at 1300 4th St, Berkeley 94710 (510-280-7660).

Directory Description: FAVA is a small, daytime lunch counter on Vine Street in North Berkeley. It is run by chefs Sylvie Osborne Calierno and Jeremy Scheiblauer, who met while cooking at Chez Panisse. Sylvie had earlier opened her own restaurant in Spain, and Jeremy led the kitchen at a San Francisco restaurant before returning to Chez Panisse. The pair took over the space long occupied by the Juice Bar Collective. Their cooking is fresh, simple and built around seasonal ingredients, and service is casual and counter-style. The relaxed setting makes FAVA an easy choice for a neighborhood lunch, and families with children are welcome.
Highlights: Chez Panisse-alumni chefs; seasonal, simply prepared lunch fare; salads; counter service; family-friendly; former Juice Bar Collective space
Hours: Tue–Sat 11am–3pm; closed Sun–Mon
Notes to Verify: The input says Middle Eastern. The official site and the sources I could read name no specific dishes, and Yelp categorizes it as Salad. Verify the cuisine label against the current menu or Instagram (@fava_onvine). No phone is listed.

Directory Description: Gather opened in 2009 on the ground floor of the David Brower Center, steps from the UC Berkeley campus. It was founded by Eric Fenster and Ari Derfel of Back to Earth Catering and has become a showcase for organic, sustainably sourced California cooking. The seasonal menu draws on dozens of local farms and ranches and is designed for omnivores, vegetarians and vegans alike. Standouts include a vegan pizza made with cashew cream and a seasonal roast chicken, served with cocktails made from sustainable spirits. The dining room is built largely from reclaimed materials, including seat cushions stitched from old leather belts. Gather serves lunch, dinner and weekend brunch, and hosts private events.
Highlights: Organic, locally sourced seasonal menu; many vegetarian and vegan dishes; vegan pizza with cashew cream; seasonal roast chicken; sustainable-spirits cocktails; reclaimed-material interior; weekend brunch; private events for 15–200
Hours: Mon–Fri 11am–2pm & 4–8:30pm; Sat–Sun 10am–2pm & 4–8:30pm
Notes to Verify: The website styles the name 'Gather in Berkeley'. It is located in the David Brower Center. Dish examples come from a 2019 Berkeleyside article, and the menu changes seasonally.

Directory Description: Gusto opened on Shattuck Avenue in January 2026 as Berkeley's first Algerian fast-food spot. Owner Abdullah Bouhafs runs it with the aim of sharing the everyday street food of his home country with a new generation. Merguez, the spiced North African sausage, is the star and comes in lamb, beef or chicken. The menu also includes Algerian-style wraps and tacos, shawarma and burgers. Traditional sweets such as maqrout, ghribiya and kunafa are made fresh daily. Everything is halal, prices are modest, and videos and photos of Algerian landscapes set the mood. Gusto offers dine-in, takeout and delivery.
Highlights: Merguez (lamb, beef or chicken); Algerian tacos and wraps; shawarma; burgers; house-made Algerian pastries (maqrout, ghribiya, kunafa, mille-feuille); 100% halal; budget-friendly
Hours: Mon–Thu 11am–9pm; Fri–Sat 11am–10pm; Sun 11am–9pm
Notes to Verify: The input says Algerian/Persian. I found no evidence of Persian dishes; every source describes it as Algerian/North African. There is no official website, only Instagram @gusto_resterant_ and Facebook. The phone was taken from the input and not independently verified. ZIP 94704 is assumed.

Cuisine: Mac and cheese / American comfort food
Directory Description: Homeroom began in Oakland in 2011 as a restaurant devoted almost entirely to macaroni and cheese. Its Berkeley outpost brings that playful concept to West Berkeley's Gilman District, in a warehouse building shared with other local food businesses. The menu offers creative takes on the comfort classic. The most popular is a Gilroy garlic mac, and there are also truffle and Buffalo chicken versions, among many others. The Berkeley location keeps late hours and is set up for pickup, delivery and catering, which makes it an easy choice for a group meal or a late-night craving.
Highlights: Gilroy garlic mac; truffle mac; Buffalo chicken mac; late-night hours; pickup, delivery and catering
Hours: Daily 11am–midnight
Notes to Verify: Confirmed as an official Berkeley location, the third Homeroom in the Bay Area. The flagship is at 400 40th St, Oakland, and there is also a location at 4007 Webster St, Oakland. The address includes Suite 130. The Berkeley site emphasizes pickup and delivery; confirm whether it offers dine-in seating.

Cuisine: Gastropub / wood-fired pizza and small plates
Directory Description: In the Wood calls itself a gastropub for the Elmwood neighborhood: a casual, contemporary place for neighbors to meet over food and drinks on College Avenue. It has been open since 2018. The kitchen is built around a wood-fired oven that turns out pizzas alongside small and large plates made with local meats, fish and produce, with vegan and gluten-free options available. The bar focuses on locally brewed craft beers and sustainable wines, and happy hours are a regular feature. In the Wood serves lunch, dinner and brunch, with indoor and patio seating as well as takeout.
Highlights: Wood-fired pizzas; small and large plates with local meats, fish and produce; vegan and gluten-free options; local craft beer and sustainable wines; happy hours; brunch; patio seating
Hours: Sun–Thu 11:30am–8:30pm; Fri–Sat 11:30am–9pm
Notes to Verify: Also styled 'In The Wood Gastropub' (delivery apps) and 'In The Wood Grill & Bar' (Instagram). The owner's name was not confirmed. Reservations are taken for parties of 6 or more.

Neighborhood: Kensington (Arlington Ave business district, just north of Berkeley)
Directory Description: Inn Kensington is a small neighborhood cafe on Arlington Avenue in Kensington, in the hills just north of Berkeley. Locals come here for a classic American breakfast and lunch. The menu leans on hearty morning favorites: homemade biscuits, corned beef hash, omelettes and scrambles, pancakes and waffles, and a chorizo breakfast for those who want some spice. The atmosphere is relaxed and family-friendly, with a cozy dining room and some outdoor seating. Guests can eat in or order takeout, and seasonal specials keep regulars coming back.
Highlights: Homemade biscuits; corned beef hash; omelettes and scrambles; corn-cilantro pancakes; waffles; chorizo breakfast; outdoor seating; dine-in or takeout
Hours: 7:30am–2:30pm; closed Tuesdays (per aggregator; verify)
Notes to Verify: It is located in Kensington (unincorporated Contra Costa County), not Berkeley proper. The official site blocks automated reading, so menu items and hours come from aggregator listings; verify them against innkensington.com. I found no owner or history information. Reports that the outdoor seating is pet-friendly are unverified.

Directory Description: Juanita & Maude is an intimate, chef-driven restaurant on San Pablo Avenue in Albany. Chef Scott Eastman, formerly chef de cuisine at Berkeley's Corso, opened it in 2017 with co-owner Ariane Owens. It is named for his grandmother Juanita and his mother Maude. The kitchen offers Eastman's personal take on American cooking: a daily-changing, ingredient-driven menu of refined comfort food that draws on influences from around the world. Diners can sit in the lively dining room, anchored by a zinc bar, or on a heated back patio. A full bar with creative cocktails, wine and beer rounds out the dinner-only experience.
Highlights: Daily-changing seasonal menu; well-known house burger; creative cocktails; zinc bar; heated back patio; private dining
Hours: Tue–Sat 5–9pm
Notes to Verify: The early menu (2018) was described as Northern Italian with Japanese touches; the restaurant now presents as American. OpenTable mentions Michelin Guide recognition for its burger, which I did not independently verify, so it was left out of the description.

Directory Description: KAOKAO Grill is an owner-run spot on College Avenue in the Elmwood that brings American-style smoked barbecue together with Asian flavors and noodle bowls. Diners come for glossy char siu pork served over rice and for hearty bowls of noodles topped with smoky brisket, balanced by cool sides like spiced eggplant salad and tangy cucumbers, with house sodas to drink. The casual, loft-like room has seating on two levels, and the kitchen also handles takeout and delivery for those who want to bring their barbecue home. It is an easygoing neighborhood choice for lunch or an early dinner.
Highlights: Smoked char siu pork; brisket noodle soup; cold eggplant salad; cucumber salad; house sodas; two-level loft-style dining room; takeout and delivery
Hours: Tue-Sun 11:30am-3pm, 4pm-8:30pm; closed Mon (per aggregator listing)
Notes to Verify: Sourcing is thin: details come mainly from aggregator listings (Wheree) and delivery platforms. No official website, owner name or press coverage found. One aggregator (goto-where) calls it 'Chinese and Indian BBQ', which conflicts with the other sources and was not used. 'Owner-run' comes from the input spreadsheet only.

Directory Description: Kiraku, whose name means "to relax," has brought the spirit of a Japanese izakaya to Telegraph Avenue since 2011. Chef Daiki Saito, who trained in French cooking in Japan before working in Bay Area sushi and yakitori kitchens, runs it with his wife, Sanae. Evenings begin with a warm towel and move through small plates and grilled skewers meant for sharing over drinks. Saito is a certified sake sommelier, and the list of sake and shochu runs deep, with a bottle-keep program for regulars and Asahi draft poured Japanese-style. Many of the stoneware dishes are made by the chef himself.
Highlights: Izakaya small plates; yakitori-style skewers; extensive sake and shochu list; bottle-keep program; Asahi draft poured Japanese-style; chef-made stoneware; dinner only; takeout via Toast
Hours: Tue-Thu 5:30pm-10pm; Fri-Sat 5:30pm-11pm
Notes to Verify: Official website title is 'Kiraku Berkeley'. Reservations through Yelp. The website does not list Sun/Mon hours, so the restaurant appears to be closed those days.

Directory Description: Korean Superette on Solano Avenue is part neighborhood market, part casual Korean eatery. It opened in 2022 in the longtime home of the restaurant Rivoli. Shelves and deli cases around the dining room hold house-made banchan, kimchi (including vegan versions), noodles and pantry staples for cooking Korean food at home. From the kitchen come comforting plates such as rice bowls with soup, tteokbokki and rotating specials like gochujang-braised pork ribs. Guests can eat inside or on the outdoor seating, or pick up ready-made meals to go. The shop also offers catering, private event space and a meal subscription.
Highlights: House-made banchan and kimchi (vegan options); rice bowls with soup; tteokbokki; rotating specials; Korean pantry goods and ready-to-eat meals; indoor and outdoor seating; catering and Bapsang Club meal subscription
Hours: Sun-Thu 11am-9pm; Fri-Sat 11am-10pm
Notes to Verify: The spreadsheet says Albany, but the business, Yelp and ordering sites all list the address as Berkeley (Solano Ave, 94707). Owner names not found. Phone taken from the input and not independently confirmed. Opening date inferred from Hungry Onion posts (open by late April 2022).

Directory Description: La Marcha Tapas Bar brings a lively Spanish spirit to San Pablo Avenue. Owner Sergio Emilio Monleón learned the rules of Valencian paella from his Spanish grandmother, and the pans that come out of the kitchen show it: classic paella mixta with prawns, chicken and chorizo, and the all-pork "tres cerditos." A long list of tapas fills out the table, from sizzling head-on garlic shrimp to salt cod croquetas with romesco and tortilla española. The MICHELIN Guide recommends it. There is an L-shaped bar with weekday happy hour, weekend brunch and late nights on Fridays and Saturdays, and groups are welcome.
Highlights: Paella mixta; 'tres cerditos' pork paella; garlic shrimp; salt cod croquetas with romesco; tortilla española; weekday happy hour; weekend brunch; late-night Fri-Sat; MICHELIN Guide recommended
Hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11am-3pm; brunch Sat-Sun 10am-3pm; dinner daily 4pm-10pm; happy hour Mon-Fri 4pm-6pm; late night Fri-Sat 10pm-12am
Notes to Verify: The MICHELIN page shows daytime-only hours, which conflicts with the restaurant's own site; hours here are from lamarchaberkeley.com. SF Chronicle gives 2015 as the founding year. Monleón also runs ghost-kitchen spinoffs (La Marcha Express, Croqueta Burger), which are not part of this listing.

Directory Description: La Note has been serving Provençal-style breakfast and lunch on Shattuck Avenue since 1997, and it has become one of Downtown Berkeley's best-loved morning spots. The kitchen is known for its pancakes, especially lemon gingerbread and oatmeal-raspberry, as well as pain perdu and omelets like the Côte Ouest filled with ratatouille. The dining room has the relaxed charm of a country bistro, and a quiet courtyard patio out back is a favorite on sunny days. Weekend lines are common, and the restaurant takes reservations through its website.
Highlights: Lemon gingerbread pancakes; oatmeal-raspberry and crème fraîche pancakes; pain perdu; Côte Ouest omelet with ratatouille; back courtyard patio; breakfast and brunch only
Hours: Mon-Fri 8am-2pm; Sat-Sun 8am-3pm
Notes to Verify: The restaurant's website lists ZIP 94707, but 2377 Shattuck Ave (Downtown) is in 94704, as other listings show; 94704 used here. Owner name not confirmed.

Directory Description: Lao Garden is chef Kanlaya Palivan's showcase for Laotian cooking on San Pablo Avenue. She briefly ran Rose Garden Uptown in Oakland while waiting on Berkeley permits, then opened here in January 2025. The menu leans into Lao classics such as nam khao (crispy rice salad wrapped in lettuce), laab gai, funky green papaya salad and kua mee Lao, alongside familiar noodles like drunken noodles. The room is bright and cheerful, with orange chairs, colorful lanterns and a wall of flowers and butterflies. There is a bar, and the restaurant serves both lunch and dinner.
Highlights: Nam khao crispy rice salad; laab gai; thum lao lao green papaya salad; kua mee Lao; drunken noodles; colorful lantern-lit dining room; full bar; lunch and dinner
Hours: Mon-Sat 11am-3pm, 5pm-9pm; Sun 12pm-3pm, 5pm-9pm (as of April 2025)
Notes to Verify: Opened January 2025 in the former Paisan space. Facebook page name is 'Lao Garden Restaurant & Bar'. Hours come from East Bay Express (April 2025) and may have changed.

Address: 10166 San Pablo Ave, El Cerrito, CA 94530
Directory Description: Larb Thai Food & Tapas takes its name from larb, the zesty minced-meat salad of northeastern Thailand's Isaan region, and that dish anchors the menu here. This small, unpretentious restaurant in a San Pablo Avenue strip mall in El Cerrito has a warm, family-run feel. Beyond larb made with meat or prawns, regulars order the crispy rice ball salad, pork hock, khao soi and well-made noodle staples like drunken noodles and pad see ew. Spice levels run from mild to true Thai heat, and the kitchen will work around dietary needs. It serves lunch and dinner for dine-in and takeout.
Highlights: Larb (meat or prawn); crispy rice ball salad; pork hock; khao soi; drunken noodles; pad Thai; adjustable spice levels; lunch and dinner
Hours: Lunch 11:30am-2:10pm, dinner 5pm-8:10pm (per DoorDash); closed Tuesdays (per Tripadvisor)
Notes to Verify: Official website could not be fetched (rate limited). Reviews name the owners as 'Ann & Paul'; not independently confirmed, so omitted from the description. Hours vary slightly between sources.

Directory Description: Li's Knife Cut Noodle is a family-run noodle house that opened on Center Street in December 2025, following its first location in San Mateo. Owner Jian Han's parents spent more than two decades making noodles in China, and their method drives the menu: dough is shaved by hand straight into boiling water, giving wide, tender, chewy strands. Bowls come in a range of homestyle preparations, with dumplings on the side, and the house offers free noodle refills for anyone still hungry. The Downtown Berkeley dining room is roomier than the original, with more than 20 tables.
Highlights: Hand-shaved knife-cut noodles; dumplings; free unlimited noodle refills; homestyle Chinese cooking; family-run; dine-in, takeout and delivery
Notes to Verify: Opened December 8, 2025 (Daily Californian). Chinese name 李面请大碗刀削面. The brand website focuses on the San Mateo location. Phone taken from the input and not independently confirmed. Hours not verified.

Directory Description: Lulu's Little Kitchen is chef Mona Leena's casual, counter-service take on the California-meets-Palestinian cooking she first served at her full-service restaurant Lulu. In early 2026 Leena reworked the Solano Avenue space into a more affordable, everyday format built around halal rice bowls, roti wraps, salads, sides and coffee, with fillings such as braised lamb, chicken kebab and falafel alongside hummus and toum fries. The bright, sunny room suits a relaxed lunch or an early dinner, and takeout is available. On weekends, brunch brings back some of Lulu's best-loved dishes, including knafeh pancakes, baklava French toast and shukaquiles.
Highlights: Braised lamb bowl; falafel and labneh bowls; roti wraps; toum fries; weekend knafeh pancakes, baklava French toast and shukaquiles
Hours: Wed-Sun 11:30am-7:30pm; closed Mon-Tue (brunch items Sat-Sun)
Notes to Verify: Formerly the full-service restaurant 'Lulu' (earlier on Camelia St in Berkeley, then 1106 Solano). Full service ended Jan 31, 2026 and the space reopened as counter-service Lulu's Little Kitchen (reopening was delayed past the planned Feb 14 date by construction). The address is in Albany, not Berkeley.

Cuisine: Modern Mexican; mezcal and tequila bar
Directory Description: Mercado 925 is a colorful Mexican restaurant and bar on University Avenue in West Berkeley, opened in 2023 by restaurateur Juan Romo, who is also behind Casa Latina and La Mission. The kitchen puts an inventive spin on regional dishes such as mole poblano tacos, enmoladas de Puebla, chiles rellenos, Baja fish tacos and Sonora-style ceviche. The bar is known for its deep list of mezcal and tequila. In 2025 the restaurant added m925, an annex with high ceilings, rattan furniture, a semi-private mezzanine and a bottle shop. There is also an upstairs terrace. Mexican brunch and weekday happy hour make it an easy fit for dates, families and small celebrations.
Highlights: Mole poblano tacos; enmoladas de Puebla; chiles rellenos; ceviche de Sonora; Baja fish tacos; mezcal and tequila list; m925 annex and bottle shop; upstairs terrace; brunch and happy hour
Hours: Per OpenTable: Sun-Mon, Tue, Thu 11am-9pm; Fri-Sat 11am-10pm (Wednesday not listed; verify)
Notes to Verify: The official website could not be fetched (rate-limited), so its hours and menu were not checked directly. The m925 market annex soft-opened in June 2025. No chef was named in any source found.

Neighborhood: Telegraph Avenue / Southside, near UC Berkeley
Directory Description: Mezzo carries on the legacy of Cafe Intermezzo, a Telegraph Avenue favorite that opened in 1983 and was lost to a fire in 2011. The cafe reopened as Mezzo in 2017, keeping the original recipes while pairing a modern look with vintage pieces saved from the old cafe. It is best known for very large salads, including the popular Chef Salad with house poppyseed dressing, as well as made-to-order sandwiches on house-made honey wheat bread and daily soups. Breakfast is served in the morning. A ramp connects Mezzo to Raleigh's Pub next door, so guests can have their sandwich with a local craft beer.
Highlights: Chef Salad with poppyseed dressing; house-made honey wheat bread; made-to-order sandwiches; soups; breakfast; connected to Raleigh's Pub
Hours: Daily 8am-9pm (closes 6:30pm Tuesdays); breakfast 8-11am
Notes to Verify: Named Best Sandwiches in Berkeley in The Daily Californian's Best of Berkeley 2020, according to Mezzo's own website. Online ordering runs through a joint Toast page with Raleigh's Pub.

Neighborhood: Telegraph Avenue / Southside, near UC Berkeley
Directory Description: Mount Everest Restaurant is a family-run Nepali and Indian restaurant on upper Telegraph Avenue, a few blocks south of the UC Berkeley campus. It opened in 2010 and is now run by the second generation of the family. It has become a regular stop for students and neighbors looking for Himalayan comfort food made with traditional recipes and fresh ingredients. The menu covers both Nepali and North Indian dishes, including steamed momo dumplings, samosas, chaat, biryani, dishes from the tandoor and a wide range of curries. The dining room is relaxed and welcoming, and the restaurant also offers takeout.
Highlights: Momos; samosas and chaat; tandoori dishes; biryani; Nepali and Indian curries
Hours: Per Visit Berkeley: Mon-Tue and Thu-Sun 11am-9:15pm; closed Wednesday
Notes to Verify: Two websites exist: mteverestberkeley.com, which Visit Berkeley links to, and mounteverestrestaurantca.com. The 2010 founding year and second-generation ownership come from the restaurant's own story page.

Neighborhood: Telegraph Avenue / Southside, near UC Berkeley
Directory Description: Noodle Dynasty is a small, busy Chinese noodle shop on Telegraph Avenue near the UC Berkeley campus. It specializes in hand-pulled noodles served in rich, slow-cooked broths. The house special beef rib noodle soup, made with a bone-in rib, is the dish most people come for. Lamb shank noodles, spicy pickled cabbage with fish, and stir-fried dishes round out the menu. Guests order on tablets, the open kitchen works quickly, and the compact dining room is usually full and noisy. At peak times a line often forms down the sidewalk, drawing students and East Bay noodle fans alike.
Highlights: House special beef rib noodle soup; lamb shank noodles; pickled cabbage and fish; hand-pulled noodles; tablet ordering; open kitchen
Hours: Tue-Sun 12-4pm and 5-8pm (per restaurant site); closed Monday
Notes to Verify: No owner names or opening date were found. The restaurant's website says it has been covered by Berkeleyside, the SF Chronicle and The Oaklandside, but those articles were not checked directly.

Directory Description: O2 Eatery is a bright breakfast and brunch spot on Solano Avenue. It opened in August 2024 in the former Delirama deli space, run by the previous owners of Sumo Sushi on San Pablo Avenue. The dated deli was fully remodeled into a calm, green-toned dining room with a closed kitchen. The menu centers on eggs, with omelets, scrambles, benedicts and breakfast sandwiches on brioche, along with a goddess breakfast bowl and croffles. A popular side is crispy potatoes finished with chimichurri. It serves breakfast and lunch only, making it a good choice for a weekend brunch or a relaxed weekday meal.
Highlights: Omelets and scrambles; eggs benedict; brioche breakfast sandwiches; goddess breakfast bowl; croffles; crispy chimichurri potatoes
Hours: Daily 8am-3pm (per East Bay Express at opening; verify)
Notes to Verify: The website's page titles say 'Albany' in some places, but the address is Berkeley 94707 on Solano Ave. The phone number comes from the input list and was not independently confirmed. The source spelled the item 'crofles'; the standard spelling is croffles.

Directory Description: Peace Natural Vegan Food is a small plant-based restaurant on Solano Avenue run by chef-owners Palden and Gyatso. It serves wholesome, organic vegan meals from a menu that changes every day with the season. Instead of a long à la carte list, diners choose a set plate. The Modest and Generous meals include soup, grains, legumes, greens, mixed vegetables and salad, while the Trio pairs soup with three dishes of the day. Momos and fresh rolls are available as starters, and the house-made desserts contain no refined sugar. Teas, kombucha, and organic vegan beer and wine complete the menu.
Highlights: Daily-changing set meals (Modest, Generous, Trio); vegan momos; fresh rolls; sugar-free house-made desserts; organic vegan beer and wine; kombucha
Hours: Daily 11am-2:30pm and 4:30-8pm (per Tripadvisor listing; verify)
Notes to Verify: No official website was confirmed; Tripadvisor shows a website link but the URL could not be seen. Owner names (Palden and Gyatso) come only from the Tripadvisor listing. DoorDash lists the cuisine as Tibetan-American, and the description leaves that label out because it could not be confirmed elsewhere. The 'prix-fixe' concept in the input corresponds to the set-meal format.

Directory Description: Phosho Dough is a Vietnamese restaurant on San Pablo Avenue in West Berkeley. It is the second location of an Oakland eatery that started on Telegraph Avenue, and it is owned by Richard Kha. The menu is built on comforting noodle soups, including lemongrass beef pho and hu tieu ga, a shredded-chicken noodle soup. Grilled pork and shrimp vermicelli bowls, crispy cha gio egg rolls and banh mi sandwiches round it out. Portions are generous and the setting is casual, so it works well for a quick lunch or an early dinner, whether eating in or taking out.
Highlights: Lemongrass beef pho (pho bo nuong); hu tieu ga chicken noodle soup; bun tom thit nuong vermicelli; banh mi thit; cha gio egg rolls
Hours: About 11am-6:40pm per DoorDash (verify)
Notes to Verify: The input calls it 'family-run', but no source confirmed that, so the description does not say it. Owner Richard Kha is named by What Now SF. The original location is at 6601 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. The Berkeley location announced its expansion in 2024 (Berkeleyside, May 2024; article not fetchable). The ZIP code (94706) was not confirmed by a source; verify it. The phone number was not independently confirmed.

Cuisine: Rotisserie chicken, house-made charcuterie and sausages; takeout deli
Neighborhood: San Pablo Ave at Solano Ave, Albany
Directory Description: Picnic is a neighborhood rotisserie and charcuterie shop at San Pablo and Solano avenues in Albany. It was founded by two neighbors, butcher-chef Susannah Schnick and chef and business lead Leslie Nishiyama. Schnick learned charcuterie at Fatted Calf and whole-animal butchery at Cafe Rouge and Clove & Hoof. The pair began by selling at local farmers markets before opening their storefront. Picnic is built around takeout, with golden rotisserie chickens, sausages, salami, pâté, porchetta and chicken liver mousse, plus salads, sides, pickles, sandwiches and a weekly-changing menu. Much of the food is made in-house from locally sourced meat.
Highlights: Rotisserie chicken; house-made sausages and salami; chicken liver mousse; porchetta; country pâté; salads, sides and sandwiches; weekly menu
Notes to Verify: The phone number conflicts: the input lists 510-570-2974, while the Solano Avenue Association lists 510-527-5358; verify. The chicken liver mousse is described as a 2019 Good Food Award 'finalist' by Berkeleyside but as a 'winner' by the Solano Avenue Association, so the description leaves this out. Berkeleyside (Nov 2018) projected a spring 2019 opening, but its Dec 2020 headline says Picnic 'brings rotisserie and charcuterie to Albany', so the actual opening may have been later. The official site could not be fetched (robots/rate-limited), and hours were not confirmed.

Cuisine: Seasonal Californian bar food; wine and cocktail bar
Directory Description: Roses on Adeline is a neighborhood bar and kitchen on South Berkeley's Adeline Corridor, built around the idea of food as a way to connect people. The evening-only menu leans seasonal and Californian, with bar favorites like a smashburger next to lighter plates such as crudo, tuna tartare, ceviche, tostadas and pasta. Drinks cover wine, beer and cocktails, and the wine list has a soft spot for chilled reds and skin-contact bottles. Guests can sit at the bar or in banquettes, and the dining room opens onto an attached garden that brings in daylight and fresh air. Walk-ins are welcome, reservations are available, and happy hour runs daily.
Highlights: Smashburger; crudo and tuna tartare; ceviche and tostadas; natural and skin-contact wines; daily happy hour; garden-side dining room; private events and buyouts
Hours: Mon-Wed 4pm-10pm; Thu 4pm-11pm; Fri-Sat 4pm-midnight; Sun 4pm-10pm (happy hour daily 4-6pm)
Notes to Verify: Owner/chef names not found in accessible sources (Berkeleyside June 2025 profile could not be fetched). Website notes an East Bay Express 'Best of the East Bay 2025' recognition; Infatuation reviewed it June 2025. No outdoor patio per website, but attached garden.

Directory Description: Sakana Sushi & Roll is a small neighborhood sushi spot on Arlington Avenue in Kensington, just over the hill from North Berkeley. The menu covers the classics, including nigiri, sashimi, chirashi and assorted moriawase platters, alongside donburi and poke bowls. Its playful side shows in the long list of special and baked rolls, such as the Lion King, which is crab and avocado under baked salmon, and a rice-free house special wrapped in pickled radish around salmon, tuna, unagi, mango and avocado. Vegetarian rolls round out the options. Guests can eat in the cozy dining room or order takeout, including party platters for sharing.
Highlights: Lion King baked roll; rice-free Sakana Special Roll wrapped in pickled radish; nigiri, sashimi and chirashi moriawase; poke and donburi bowls; vegetarian rolls; party platters for takeout
Hours: Mon-Sat 11:45am-2:15pm and 4:30pm-8:15pm; Sun 3:30pm-8:15pm (per online ordering site)
Notes to Verify: Full name is 'Sakana Sushi & Roll' (Yelp: 'Sakana Sushi and Roll'); some listings (DoorDash, Tripadvisor) shorten it to 'Sakana Sushi'. Official site is an online-ordering site; no owner/chef or backstory found. Do not confuse with Sakana Sushi in Reno, NV.

Neighborhood: Albany (San Pablo Avenue, on the Berkeley border)
Directory Description: Sam's Log Cabin is a longtime breakfast and brunch destination housed in a genuine log cabin on San Pablo Avenue in Albany. The building dates to 1930, when it was ordered as a kit from a Sears catalog, and it has reportedly served as a speakeasy and a bookies' hangout along the way. Today the kitchen, run by co-owner and chef Rhasaan Fernandez with partner Mike Daillak, turns out hearty morning plates with Southern and Californian touches: chilaquiles with house-made chips, braised collard greens with poached eggs and cornbread, seasonal pancake specials and a fried chicken sandwich. Seating is outdoors on the patio, and the vibe is relaxed, homey and dog-friendly.
Highlights: Chilaquiles with house-made tortilla chips; pork-braised collard greens with poached eggs and cornbread; daily seasonal pancakes; fried chicken sandwich; 1930 Sears-kit log cabin; outdoor patio; dog-friendly
Notes to Verify: Owner and dish details come from a 2018 Berkeleyside profile; menu items may have changed since. Outdoor-only patio seating per the input brief (not independently verified); DogTrekker lists it as dog-friendly. 2018 hours were Tue-Fri 7am-2pm, Sat-Sun 8am-2pm, but current hours unverified so left blank. Walk-in only (no reservations) as of 2018. Address is Albany, not Berkeley.

Neighborhood: Southwest Berkeley (Dwight Way near San Pablo Ave)
Directory Description: Tanzie's is a chef-owned Berkeley cafe that gives brunch a Northern Thai accent. Chef Krissana "Tanz" Tussanaprasit, a Kin Khao alum who also ran a restaurant in Chiang Mai, opened it in early 2024 with partner Jezreel "Jae" Rojas, a veteran of Kin Khao and La Cocina. Many recipes come from Tanz's family. Standouts include pa tong go, Thai-style beignets with sweetened condensed milk; "lava eggs," soft scrambled eggs over rice with savory toppings such as nam prik ong; Thai spiced sausage; and a jasmine Thai tea chia bowl, plus matcha drinks. The small, cottage-like space has cozy nooks, plenty of plants and a fireplace. Reservations are taken through Tock.
Highlights: Pa tong go (Thai beignets); lava eggs with nam prik ong; Thai spiced sausage; jasmine Thai tea chia bowl; matcha drinks; cottage-like room with fireplace
Hours: Mon and Thu 10am-2pm; Fri-Sun 8:30am-2pm; closed Tue-Wed (per website)
Notes to Verify: CUISINE DISCREPANCY: the brief says 'Filipino-inspired', but every source (website, SF Chronicle, Berkeleyside, Broke-Ass Stuart) describes Tanzie's as Thai, specifically Chiang Mai/Northern Thai; description written as Thai. Named to SF Chronicle's Top 25 new Bay Area restaurants list (Oct 2024). Dinner service was added Dec 2024, but the current website lists only daytime hours, so dinner may have ended. Owners have since opened a second concept, Nudi Blue (SF Chronicle).

Directory Description: Tarocco is a sunny weekday lunch cafe on Ninth Street in West Berkeley, modeled on the relaxed counter bars of Barcelona. It began in 2020 as a pandemic meal-delivery service and opened a physical location in 2022. Owner Sequoia Del Hoyo, co-founder of Sequoia Diner, runs it with chef Jason Botterill, who previously cooked at Chez Panisse and London's River Cafe. Guests choose from a counter of composed seasonal salads and ready-made Mediterranean dishes built on produce from local farms, then eat in the bright, rustic dining room or take their food to go. Tarocco also offers catering, weekend private events and Club Tarocco, a weekly meal subscription.
Highlights: Composed seasonal salads from local farms; Barcelona-style counter service; sunlit rustic dining room; Club Tarocco weekly meal subscription; catering and weekend private events
Hours: Mon-Fri 11am-2:30pm; weekends reserved for private events
Notes to Verify: Official styling is all caps, 'TAROCCO'. Broke-Ass Stuart (Feb 2024) lists Del Hoyo and Botterill as co-owners; the website calls Del Hoyo owner and Botterill chef. Switched from table service to counter service in Nov 2023. Cuisine is described as Mediterranean/Barcelona-inspired as well as Californian.

Cuisine: Cafe: organic coffee, tea, light fare and weekend brunch
Neighborhood: West Berkeley (Addison St at Strawberry Creek Park)
Directory Description: The Hidden Café is a small, bohemian-feeling daytime cafe tucked into a building beside Strawberry Creek Park in West Berkeley, which makes finding it part of the appeal. It is a relaxed place to linger over coffee or tea, with indoor tables and outdoor seating in a leafy, park-like setting. The drinks menu goes beyond espresso to include turmeric lattes, chai and matcha, while the kitchen offers pastries and treats such as a sweet potato brownie, along with a rotating weekend brunch. The cafe also has ties to local artists and musicians, adding a creative, community-minded feel to this neighborhood hideaway.
Highlights: Organic coffee and oat cappuccinos; turmeric latte, chai and matcha; sweet potato brownie; rotating weekend brunch; indoor and outdoor seating by Strawberry Creek Park; artist and musician features
Hours: Tue-Sun 8:30am-5pm; closed Mon (per joe coffee listing)
Notes to Verify: The official website could not be fetched directly; details come from the joe coffee listing, search-result titles and site page names (e.g. 'The Hidden Kitchen', 'Artists and Musicians'). The 'organic coffee' claim comes from the input brief and was not independently verified. Phone has a 415 area code despite the Berkeley location. Owner names not found (Berkeleyside 2019 profile not fetchable).

Directory Description: Tipsy Yeti Restaurant & Bar brings a lively, modern take on Nepali cooking to San Pablo Avenue. Owners Sujan Shrestha and Rubin Sainju opened it in 2025 in a longtime restaurant space, pairing the flavors of Kathmandu with a Californian, comfort-food streak. Momo lead the menu, filled with paneer, chicken, lamb or bison and also served in jhol broth, alongside choila (spiced duck with beaten rice), goat curry and chili chicken. Crossover dishes like a bison burger, Himalayan pizza and tornado fries fill out the list. A full bar pours signature cocktails, wine and mocktails, and live music on weekends keeps the family-friendly dining room busy.
Highlights: Momo (paneer, chicken, lamb or bison) and jhol momo; duck choila with beaten rice; goat curry; bison burger; Himalayan pizza; signature cocktails and mocktails; weekend live music
Notes to Verify: Opened 2025 (Berkeleyside Feb 2025 opening roundup; WhatNow reported owners Sujan Shrestha and Rubin Sainju). Same address was previously Longbranch (Saloon) and earlier Sea Salt, per Yelp 'closed' listings. Note the misspelled look-alike domain typsiyeti.com in search results; official site is tipsyeti.com. Hours not listed on website.

Directory Description: Via del Corso is a North Berkeley Italian trattoria on Shattuck Avenue, in the space long home to the beloved Tuscan spot Corso. When Corso closed during the pandemic, Berkeley-born restaurateur Peter Chastain revived it under a new name borrowed from a grand boulevard in Rome. The kitchen draws on central Italy and other regions, and it brought back some of Corso's best-loved dishes, including bistecca alla Fiorentina and pollo al burro, chicken in a rich butter sauce. The team's opening lineup included veterans of Walnut Creek's Prima. It is a relaxed, dinner-only place for wine, pasta and long meals with family and friends, and it takes reservations.
Highlights: Bistecca alla Fiorentina; pollo al burro (Corso's butter chicken); central Italian pastas; Italian wine; dinner service with reservations
Hours: Sun and Tue-Thu 5pm-9pm; Fri-Sat 5pm-10pm; closed Mon (per website)
Notes to Verify: Successor to Corso (2008-2020, owners Roscoe Skipper and Wendy Brucker). Staff details (chef Massimo Orlando, GM Marco Penitenti, both from Prima) come from the 2021 Berkeleyside reopening article and may be out of date, so they are left out of the description apart from the Prima connection. It has been open since roughly 2021/2022, so 'longtime' in the brief refers mostly to Corso's legacy.
